_doc: Category-3 (Grains, Cereals, and Rice Products) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-cat1.mjs — HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial limits). Numbers come ONLY from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, selected per subcategory by explicit scope regex and the strictest applicable credible sovereign-government maximum. Occurrence evidence is descriptive and cannot select an initial limit. Rice and non-rice rows remain separate where government rules distinguish their matrices; later tightening can occur only through the eligible HMTc certified-lot Standards Ratchet.
_method_note: native_basis is as_sold (dry) for every solid grain product; rice-beverages is as_consumed (liquid). reconstitution_8to1 is false everywhere (no product in this category is reconstituted from a powder concentrate). exclude_as_consumed drops prepared-state MLs from dry subcategories. Rice-product subcategories inherit applicable general cereal Pb/Cd/Ni/tHg limits and rice-specific inorganic-arsenic limits where the government source expressly covers that matrix.
_scope_note: Exclusions use PRODUCT-HEADED tokens, never bare 'rice'/'oil'/'durum', because register scopes carry 'except X' and 'including X' clauses: a bare 'rice' exclude wrongly kills 'cereals including wheat and rice' (IL tHg 30) and 'cereals except durum/rice/...' (EU Ni 800); a bare 'oil' exclude wrongly kills 'rice and derivatives except oil'. Legume/pulse/bean/soy are excluded from every subcategory because legumes are a distinct food group regulated separately; this also removes the Panama Decreto 467/2007 Cd 'cereals, legumes, and leguminous vegetables' 10 ug/kg row, a suspected units artifact (same decree sets Pb cereals at the 200 consensus) flagged for source verification and quarantine in the audit.
_read_across_canon: Cr = total-chromium reflex-speciation not-material (Cr-VI never a panel number). Sn = canned-only not-material (tin migrates from tinplate; canned grain products route to Cat 7). Al = confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv; no government sets a grain Al ML anywhere; leavened/baked Al is permitted-additive-derived, regulated by additive ADI). iAs on non-rice subcategories = not-material (arsenic does not hyperaccumulate in non-rice cereals; no government sets a non-rice grain iAs ML).

Cr.label: Conservative sovereign read-across from China GB 2762 total chromium 2000 ug/kg for milk powder to dry cereal/grain products. The matrix differs, so the source remains explicitly classified as read-across; Cr(VI) is controlled separately by reflex speciation.

iAs.control: Inorganic arsenic does not hyperaccumulate in wheat, corn, or other non-rice cereals as it does in rice; no loaded government source sets an iAs ML for a non-rice grain or flour. Rice-specific iAs limits are not transferred to this distinct matrix.
iAs.reference_method: iAs by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802) on any lot flagged for arsenic screening; non-rice grain occurrence is characteristically < LOQ.

Cr-VI.control: Cr-VI (hexavalent chromium): No government sets a total-chromium ML for grain/cereal products in any jurisdiction; cereal-matrix Cr is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the matrix. Firm control: reflex speciation — any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope-dilution; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

Sn.control: Every government tin ML in the register is scoped to canned/tin-coated product; tin migrates from tinplate. Flour is not sold in tinplate, so tin is not a material contaminant. Canned grain products route to Category 7 and carry the tin flag there.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; apply species-specific HPLC-ICP-MS for arsenic or GC/HPLC-ICP-MS for methylmercury when the stated control triggers.

Al.label: read-across: China GB 2760-2024 baked-foods Al 100 mg/kg (self-rising/leavened subset)

MeHg.control: No government sets a methylmercury ML for any grain, cereal, or rice product in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Mercury in this matrix is controlled by the total-mercury ML (30 ug/kg, Israel FCS-2016), which bounds the methylmercury fraction. Rice can accumulate trace methylmercury via paddy-soil methylation in point-source-contaminated growing regions, but that fraction is bounded by the total-mercury control and no methylmercury ML exists to look up.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 only on a lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ML; grain MeHg is characteristically < LOQ.

Pb.control: Confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv): no government sets a lead ML specific to rice-based drinks; the EU 2023/915 beverage lead framework does not enumerate a rice-drink row. Lead is material in a rice-derived beverage but unregulated by ML; literature-baseline governs. iAs is the binding Tier-1 analyte for this subcategory.
Pb.reference_method: Pb by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid.

Cd.control: Confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv): no government sets a cadmium ML specific to rice-based drinks. Material but unregulated by ML; literature-baseline governs.
Cd.reference_method: Cd by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid.

tHg.control: Mercury does not accumulate in a rice-derived beverage; the only cereal mercury MLs are dry-basis and no government sets a rice-drink mercury ML. Not a material contaminant in this matrix.
tHg.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; apply species-specific HPLC-ICP-MS for arsenic or GC/HPLC-ICP-MS for methylmercury when the stated control triggers.

Cr-VI.control: Cr-VI (hexavalent chromium): No total-Cr ML for rice beverages; reflex speciation control on the as-consumed liquid.

Ni.control: The EU 2024/1987 nickel MLs are scoped to cereal grains as commodities and to juices/nectars, not to a rice-based drink; no government sets a rice-drink nickel ML. Not a binding cell.
Ni.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; apply species-specific HPLC-ICP-MS for arsenic or GC/HPLC-ICP-MS for methylmercury when the stated control triggers.

Al.control: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for a rice-based beverage. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric Al limit for this exact cell; external plant-milk occurrence cannot supply the number.
Al.reference_method: Screen total Al by ICP-MS on the as-consumed beverage and document aluminium-containing additives or processing aids; investigate elevated results and comply with all market laws.

MeHg.control: No government sets a methylmercury ML for a rice-based beverage in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Mercury does not accumulate in a rice-derived beverage and is not a material contaminant in this matrix.
MeHg.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; apply species-specific HPLC-ICP-MS for arsenic or GC/HPLC-ICP-MS for methylmercury when the stated control triggers.

tAs.control: No government sets a total-arsenic ML for a rice-based beverage in any jurisdiction; the binding arsenic control for this subcategory is the inorganic-arsenic ML (30 ug/kg, EU 2023/915 non-alcoholic rice drinks). A dry "rice and derivatives" total-arsenic ceiling is not comparable at face value to a dilute as-consumed beverage, and total arsenic adds no ceiling beyond the inorganic-arsenic limit here.
tAs.reference_method: tAs by ICP-MS on the as-consumed liquid; speciate to iAs on any elevated total-arsenic result.
